Folks —

Reviewed the proposed exhibit. High-level legal/finance concerns:
- 99.95% unconditional is material exposure. We should gate the higher SLA behind (a) committed reserved capacity and (b) an acceptance period (as proposed).
- For latency SLOs, p95 120ms measured at Redwood’s API gateway is more defensible than trying to guarantee client-side observed latency (network variance). We should specify measurement point and exclude 3rd-party network outages.
- Service credits tiering is OK but must include an annual cap (proposed in internal approach). Also add a clause limiting credits via offset vs cash for a defined period.
- Require that any SLO exceptions be approved by a member of executive leadership (VP/GM) and Finance (to accept credit liability).

Suggested redlines (attached sla_term_redline.docx):
- Add clause: "SLA_Addendum becomes effective only upon completed performance acceptance testing as specified in Appendix A."
- Measurement: define "API Gateway p95" and sampling windows.
- Liability cap: credits capped at 5% of annual contract value; exclude credits for scheduled maintenance and force majeure.

I’m OK to sign off on routing to Evelyn for final approval if Sales is comfortable with the economics (Marissa).

-Jonas
Senior Counsel, Contracts
